{
  "rules": [
    "Systematic Underestimation of Bullish Breakouts: The model consistently fails to capture the magnitude of upward price spikes (e.g., the rise from ~80 to >95), forecasting only a slow, linear drift. Correction: Apply a non-linear upward adjustment factor when the 3-day price momentum exceeds 5% or when sentiment history shows a cluster of positive signals (0.20+)."
  ,
    "Excessive Lag in Trend Reversal: Forecasts lag significantly behind the true trend, often predicting a continuation of the previous low before the actual breakout occurs. Correction: Reduce the forecast horizon smoothing parameter to increase responsiveness to recent price changes, specifically when the current price deviates more than 3% from the 10-day moving average."
  ,
    "Failure to Price in Sentiment-Driven Volatility: Positive sentiment scores (0.20, 0.33) are ignored by the model, which maintains a flat trajectory regardless of sentiment spikes. Correction: Multiply the forecast slope by a sentiment multiplier (e.g., 1.5x for scores > 0.20) to account for the market's tendency to overreact to positive news in this specific period."
  ,
    "Mean Reversion Overshoot on the Upside: The model assumes a return to the mean (~85) after a spike, whereas the true outcome sustains higher levels (95-100). Correction: Shift the long-term mean reversion target upward by 10-15% during confirmed bull phases to prevent premature downward corrections in the forecast."
  ,
    "Horizon-Specific Decay Error: The error gap widens as the forecast horizon extends, indicating the model underestimates the duration of the rally. Correction: Extend the forecast duration of the upward trend by 5-7 days beyond the initial breakout signal before introducing any mean reversion logic."
  ]
}
